{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdM6NbyMbL2AgceGm332k","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TpaoBQfGqzmtm1tdp3xC3s","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/qa-quiz-004/2026-07-24T150848Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Mobile WalletConnect deep-linking: why \"Stake\" does nothing, why the patch broke it, and the correct pattern\n\n## 1. Why nothing auto-opened before the patch\n\n`writeContractAsync` does not \"open a wallet.\" Over a WalletConnect v2 (WCv2)\nsession, it builds an `eth_sendTransaction` JSON-RPC request and **publishes it\nto the WalletConnect relay** — an encrypted message pushed over a websocket to\nthe relay server. The wallet holds a persistent relay subscription, so Rainbow\n*receives* the request almost immediately and queues it internally. That is why,\nwhen the user manually switches to Rainbow, the signing prompt is already sitting\nthere. The request landed fine. Nothing was broken on the transport.\n\nThe missing piece is **foregrounding**. On mobile the dApp runs in a browser tab\nand the wallet is a separate, backgrounded native app. iOS/Android do **not** let\na backgrounded app pull itself to the foreground when a websocket message arrives.\nThe only thing that can bring Rainbow forward is the app currently in the\nforeground — the browser — navigating to the wallet's **deep link**\n(`rainbow://` / a universal link). That navigation counts as a user-initiated\napp switch, which the OS honors.\n\nRainbowKit/WCv2 are *supposed* to fire that redirect automatically using the\nwallet's redirect metadata stored on the session (`peer.metadata.redirect`).\nOn the initial pairing it does (that's the QR/deep-link handoff). On **subsequent\nsession requests** this auto-redirect is unreliable and frequently doesn't fire —\nolder `@walletconnect` versions, missing `redirect` metadata, or the request\noriginating outside a fresh user gesture. Result: the request is on the relay,\nRainbow has it, but no one told the OS to surface Rainbow. Tap → \"nothing happens.\"\n\n## 2. Why the patch made it worse\n\n```js\nwindow.location.href = \"rainbow://\";   // runs first, synchronously\nawait writeContractAsync(...);          // runs second — or not at all\n```\n\nTwo problems, both caused by inverting the order:\n\n- **You open the wallet before the request exists.** At the instant\n  `location.href` fires, `writeContractAsync` has not run, so nothing has been\n  published to the relay. Rainbow foregrounds and finds an **empty queue** —\n  literally nothing to sign.\n- **Foregrounding Rainbow backgrounds the browser tab, which pauses its JS.**\n  Mobile browsers throttle/suspend background tabs: the event loop and the relay\n  websocket stall. So the `writeContractAsync` publish that was supposed to run\n  \"next\" is delayed or never completes while the tab is backgrounded. Even once\n  the request eventually goes out, Rainbow is already open and showing nothing.\n\nSo the patch reliably wins the race it should lose: wallet first, request never.\nBefore the patch the request at least arrived (just without foregrounding);\nafter the patch you broke the transport too.\n\n## 3. The correct pattern\n\n### Ordering — fire the request, *don't* await it, then deep-link\n\n`writeContractAsync` only resolves **after** the user approves in the wallet — it\nreturns the tx hash post-signature. So you can never `await` it before opening the\nwallet; that's a deadlock (the wallet must open for the user to sign, but you'd be\nwaiting for the signature before opening). Instead:\n\n```js\nasync function onStake() {\n  if (!shouldDeepLink()) {\n    return writeContractAsync(stakeArgs);   // desktop/injected: just send\n  }\n\n  const scheme = await getWalletRedirect(); // from the session, see below\n\n  // start the request — this publishes to the relay — but do NOT await yet\n  const txPromise = writeContractAsync(stakeArgs);\n\n  // give the relay publish a moment, then foreground the wallet\n  setTimeout(() => {\n    if (scheme) window.location.href = scheme;\n  }, 200);\n\n  return txPromise; // await elsewhere for the hash / receipt\n}\n```\n\nKey point: the JSON-RPC request is published to the relay early in the\n`writeContractAsync` lifecycle, *before* the promise resolves. The short delay\nlets that publish happen, then you foreground a wallet that already has the\nrequest queued.\n\n### The delay and why its length is bounded on both sides\n\n~150–300 ms. It is a compromise between two hard constraints:\n\n- **Lower bound:** the request must reach the relay before Rainbow foregrounds,\n  or you recreate the patch's \"empty queue\" bug. A few hundred ms covers the\n  serialize + websocket publish.\n- **Upper bound:** mobile browsers only allow a programmatic app-open\n  (`location.href` to a custom scheme) while the **transient user activation**\n  from the tap is still live. Wait too long and the browser treats the navigation\n  as un-gestured and silently blocks it — the deep link does nothing. Keep it well\n  under a second.\n\nToo short → wallet opens to nothing. Too long → deep link ignored. ~200 ms sits\nin the middle.\n\n### Which scheme to open — never hardcode `rainbow://`\n\n`connector.id === \"walletConnect\"` for **every** wallet connected via WC —\nMetaMask, Trust, Coinbase, Rainbow all report the same id. It tells you the\n*transport*, not the *wallet*. Hardcoding `rainbow://` sends MetaMask users to\nRainbow (or nowhere).\n\nRead the wallet's own redirect metadata off the live session:\n\n```js\nasync function getWalletRedirect() {\n  const provider = await connector.getProvider();\n  const redirect = provider?.session?.peer?.metadata?.redirect;\n  // prefer the universal link (more reliable on iOS), fall back to native scheme\n  return redirect?.universal || redirect?.native || null;\n}\n```\n\n`native` is the custom scheme (`rainbow://`); `universal` is an https universal\nlink (`https://rnbwapp.com/...`). Universal links are generally more reliable on\niOS, so prefer them when present.\n\n### When to skip the deep link entirely\n\n- **Not a WalletConnect connection** — injected/extension (`connector.id`\n  `injected`/`metaMask`), Coinbase in-app, etc. There's no separate app to\n  foreground; the provider is in-page.\n- **In-app / embedded wallet browser** — the dApp is loaded *inside* MetaMask's,\n  Coinbase's, or Rainbow's own browser. The wallet is already the host and injects\n  its provider; deep-linking would try to leave the in-app browser. Detect via an\n  injected provider being present.\n- **Desktop, including desktop WalletConnect (QR)** — on a QR pairing the wallet\n  is on a *different device*; opening a scheme on the desktop is meaningless.\n  Gate on mobile user-agent / platform.\n- **No redirect metadata on the session** (`peer.metadata.redirect` missing/empty)\n  — you don't know the scheme, so don't guess. Skip rather than fire a blank/wrong\n  scheme that just blanks the page.\n\n```js\nfunction shouldDeepLink() {\n  return isMobile()                       // not desktop / not QR pairing\n      && connector?.id === \"walletConnect\"// WC transport, not injected/in-app\n      && !window.ethereum?.isMetaMask;    // not inside an in-app wallet browser\n}\n```\n\n## TL;DR\n\nThe request was always reaching Rainbow over the relay; what was missing was\nforegrounding, which only a deep link from the foreground browser can do. The\npatch deep-linked *before* creating the request (and backgrounded the tab that\nstill had to send it), so Rainbow opened to an empty queue. The fix: fire\n`writeContractAsync` without awaiting, wait ~200 ms so the request reaches the\nrelay while staying inside the tap's activation window, then open the scheme —\nread from the session's `peer.metadata.redirect`, never hardcoded — and skip the\ndeep link on desktop, injected/in-app, and metadata-less sessions.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5644,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5644},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ebc719ed-f34e-4ce9-b2c0-53f15d60d15e","uuid":"1c903bbf-43ad-4c71-a7bf-3df6b2fb9f61","timestamp":"2026-07-24T15:10:22.613Z","request_id":"req_011CdM6NaWZ713KFSNxD39j8"}

So you can never `await` it before opening the\nwallet; that's a deadlock (the wallet must open for the user to sign, but you'd be\nwaiting for the signature before opening). Instead:\n\n```js\nasync function onStake() {\n  if (!shouldDeepLink()) {\n    return writeContractAsync(stakeArgs);   // desktop/injected: just send\n  }\n\n  const scheme = await getWalletRedirect(); // from the session, see below\n\n  // start the request — this publishes to the relay — but do NOT await yet\n  const txPromise = writeContractAsync(stakeArgs);\n\n  // give the relay publish a moment, then foreground the wallet\n  setTimeout(() => {\n    if (scheme) window.location.href = scheme;\n  }, 200);\n\n  return txPromise; // await elsewhere for the hash / receipt\n}\n```\n\nKey point: the JSON-RPC request is published to the relay early in the\n`writeContractAsync` lifecycle, *before* the promise resolves. The short delay\nlets that publish happen, then you foreground a wallet that already has the\nrequest queued.\n\n### The delay and why its length is bounded on both sides\n\n~150–300 ms. It is a compromise between two hard constraints:\n\n- **Lower bound:** the request must reach the relay before Rainbow foregrounds,\n  or you recreate the patch's \"empty queue\" bug. A few hundred ms covers the\n  serialize + websocket publish.\n- **Upper bound:** mobile browsers only allow a programmatic app-open\n  (`location.href` to a custom scheme) while the **transient user activation**\n  from the tap is still live. Wait too long and the browser treats the navigation\n  as un-gestured and silently blocks it — the deep link does nothing. Keep it well\n  under a second.\n\nToo short → wallet opens to nothing. Too long → deep link ignored. ~200 ms sits\nin the middle.\n\n### Which scheme to open — never hardcode `rainbow://`\n\n`connector.id === \"walletConnect\"` for **every** wallet connected via WC —\nMetaMask, Trust, Coinbase, Rainbow all report the same id. It tells you the\n*transport*, not the *wallet*. Hardcoding `rainbow://` sends MetaMask users to\nRainbow (or nowhere).\n\nRead the wallet's own redirect metadata off the live session:\n\n```js\nasync function getWalletRedirect() {\n  const provider = await connector.getProvider();\n  const redirect = provider?.session?.peer?.metadata?.redirect;\n  // prefer the universal link (more reliable on iOS), fall back to native scheme\n  return redirect?.universal || redirect?.native || null;\n}\n```\n\n`native` is the custom scheme (`rainbow://`); `universal` is an https universal\nlink (`https://rnbwapp.com/...`). Universal links are generally more reliable on\niOS, so prefer them when present.\n\n### When to skip the deep link entirely\n\n- **Not a WalletConnect connection** — injected/extension (`connector.id`\n  `injected`/`metaMask`), Coinbase in-app, etc. There's no separate app to\n  foreground; the provider is in-page.\n- **In-app / embedded wallet browser** — the dApp is loaded *inside* MetaMask's,\n  Coinbase's, or Rainbow's own browser. The wallet is already the host and injects\n  its provider; deep-linking would try to leave the in-app browser. Detect via an\n  injected provider being present.\n- **Desktop, including desktop WalletConnect (QR)** — on a QR pairing the wallet\n  is on a *different device*; opening a scheme on the desktop is meaningless.\n  Gate on mobile user-agent / platform.\n- **No redirect metadata on the session** (`peer.metadata.redirect` missing/empty)\n  — you don't know the scheme, so don't guess. Skip rather than fire a blank/wrong\n  scheme that just blanks the page.\n\n```js\nfunction shouldDeepLink() {\n  return isMobile()                       // not desktop / not QR pairing\n      && connector?.id === \"walletConnect\"// WC transport, not injected/in-app\n      && !window.ethereum?.isMetaMask;    // not inside an in-app wallet browser\n}\n```\n\n## TL;DR\n\nThe request was always reaching Rainbow over the relay; what was missing was\nforegrounding, which only a deep link from the foreground browser can do. The\npatch deep-linked *before* creating the request (and backgrounded the tab that\nstill had to send it), so Rainbow opened to an empty queue. The fix: fire\n`writeContractAsync` without awaiting, wait ~200 ms so the request reaches the\nrelay while staying inside the tap's activation window, then open the scheme —\nread from the session's `peer.metadata.redirect`, never hardcoded — and skip the\ndeep link on desktop, injected/in-app, and metadata-less sessions.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
